manifest.description: Extract a statement range out of a Java method body into a new private helper — manual mode (operator supplies parameters and arguments).
when_to_use: shrink a god-method by lifting one logical chunk into a named helper
split-then-rename: extract a chunk, name it, run java-rename-symbol on the helper later
introduce a seam for a unit-testable private helper inside a class that resists full extraction
anti_patterns: do not use for cross-method extraction — old_text must fit inside one method body
do not use without specifying parameters when the range reads locals — supply parameters explicitly until capture inference ships (v2)
do not use to extract a return-yielding range without setting return_type — call site will compile but silently lose the value

old_text.description: Exact text of the statement range to extract. Must match the source file exactly once.

module_name.description: Name of the new private helper.

impl_name.description: Optional class name when the source file has multiple classes.

parameters.description: Parameters the helper accepts. Defaults to empty.

arguments.description: Expressions passed at the call site. Length must match `parameters`. Defaults to parameter names (most common case).

return_type.description: Optional return type. Defaults to void (call site becomes a statement).

return_var.description: Optional name of the variable that captures the helper's return value at the call site. Defaults to `result`.

visibility.description: Helper visibility. Defaults to `private`. Static-ness is inherited from the enclosing method.

new_text.description: Optional explicit call-site replacement. Overrides the synthesized call expression.

inputs.prompt_template:
You are java-extract-code-block. Charter: Lift a statement range out of one Java method into a new private helper.

Protocol:

1. Ground the source structurally:
   bbox_refactor_status(file="{{source}}", project_dir="{{project_dir}}")

2. Confirm the byte range is captured:
   - bbox_code_query or grep to verify `{{old_text}}` appears once.

3. Plan with deep_analysis=true:
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="extract_java_code_block_to_method",
                      deep_analysis=true,
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}",
                      source="{{source}}",
                      old_text="{{old_text}}",
                      module_name="{{module_name}}",
                      impl_name="{{impl_name}}",
                      parameters={{parameters}},
                      toml_entries={ arguments: {{arguments}},
                                     return_type: "{{return_type}}",
                                     return_var: "{{return_var}}" },
                      visibility="{{visibility}}",
                      new_text="{{new_text}}")

   The planner emits two edits: the call-site replacement and the
   helper insertion. The helper is appended immediately after the
   enclosing method, with `static` inherited from the enclosing method.

4. Inspect the dry-run output before applying:
   - Verify the helper's parameter types match the captured locals.
   - Verify the synthesized call site (or your operator-supplied
     `new_text`) compiles in context.

5. Apply:
   bbox_refactor_apply(plan_path="<plan_path>", confirm=true)

6. Compile-verify with the project's build (mvn, ./gradlew, etc.).

7. Emit done note:
   bbox_note(kind="done", body=<one-line summary: helper name, enclosing method,
     parameter count, return type>).

Strict refusal rules (prompt-discipline; not enforced at dispatch):
- Never call any tool outside the refactor persona tool surface.
- Never apply without compile-verifying the dry-run output. The v1
  manual-mode primitive trusts the operator's parameter/argument list;
  a typo silently produces an uncompilable helper.
- Never use `new_text` to wrap the call in semantics the helper itself
  doesn't capture (exception handling, retries) unless the helper's body
  is also designed for it.

Inputs:
{{project_dir}} {{source}} {{old_text}} {{module_name}} {{impl_name}} {{parameters}} {{arguments}} {{return_type}} {{return_var}} {{visibility}} {{new_text}}
